I am here in Afar, where the rains are short and the land is dry. I plant sorghum because it can stand the heat and the little water we get — maize would die here. I have no money for the fertilizer bags from town, and the cooperative is far. My father planted his sorghum with seed from last year's harvest and a bit of goat manure, and that is what I will do too. The neighbors here do the same — we cannot risk shillings on chemical fertilizer when the rain may not even come.

I keep some goats and a few cattle, so I have manure to scatter on the plot before planting. The seed I save from my best heads last harvest. Pests like the stalk borer come some years but I have no money for sprays — I just pull the bad plants. There is no river close enough to bring water to my plot, so I wait for the rains like everyone else. My wife and my older boy help me with the weeding and the harvest, and if the weeding is heavy I may call a cousin for two or three days and give him food and a small payment.
